Highlights:
MP में बारिश और ठंडी हवाओं से बढ़ी ठंडक।
दिन और रात के तापमान में आई गिरावट।
पूर्वी मध्य प्रदेश के कई जिलों में आंधी-बारिश का अलर्ट।
नवंबर के दूसरे सप्ताह से बढ़ सकती है ठंड।
MP Weather News : मध्य प्रदेश में बेमौसम बारिश और तेज हवाओं ने मौसम का मिजाज बदल दिया है। दिन में धूप की तपिश कम होने के साथ ठंडक बढ़ने लगी है। पिछले 4 दिनों के दौरान राज्य के कुछ हिस्सों में अधिकतम तापमान 7 से 8 डिग्री सेल्सियस तक नीचे आ चुका है। रात के तापमान में भी गिरावट दर्ज की जा रही है। मौसम में आए इस बदलाव के बीच लोगों को अब नवंबर की ठंड का एहसास होने लगा है।
मौसम विभाग के पूर्वानुमान के मुताबिक आज प्रदेश के पूर्वी हिस्सों में गरज-चमक और तेज हवाओं के साथ बारिश की संभावना है। जबलपुर, नरसिंहपुर, छिंदवाड़ा, पांढुर्णा, सिवनी, बालाघाट, मंडला, डिंडौरी, कटनी, उमरिया, अनूपपुर, शहडोल, मैहर, सीधी और सिंगरौली में मौसम का असर देखने को मिल सकता है।
इससे पहले रविवार को भी प्रदेश के कई इलाकों में मौसम बदला रहा। सिंगरौली, सीधी, रीवा, मऊगंज, सतना, अनूपपुर, शहडोल, उमरिया, डिंडौरी, छिंदवाड़ा, सिवनी, मंडला, बालाघाट, मैहर और पांढुर्णा में कुछ स्थानों पर गरज-चमक के साथ हल्की बारिश और बूंदाबांदी हुई। बारिश के कारण दिन के तापमान में गिरावट आई है।
मध्य प्रदेश में ठंड बढ़ने के साथ ही पिछले 48 घंटे में चंबल, रीवा, शहडोल और सागर संभाग में अधिकतम तापमान 5.3 से 7.7 डिग्री सेल्सियस तक गिरा है। वहीं राजधानी भोपाल, इंदौर, नर्मदापुरम, उज्जैन, ग्वालियर और जबलपुर संभाग में पारा 4.9 डिग्री तक नीचे आया। रात में भी तापमान 1 से 2 डिग्री सेल्सियस कम हुआ है।
रविवार रात दमोह में न्यूनतम तापमान 14.5 डिग्री सेल्सियस दर्ज किया गया। अमरकंटक में यह 15.1 डिग्री, भोपाल में 15.2 डिग्री, शाजापुर के गिरवर में 15.4 डिग्री और बालाघाट के मलाजखंड में 15.8 डिग्री सेल्सियस रहा। इन आंकड़ों से प्रदेश में रात के समय बढ़ती ठंड का अंदाजा लगाया जा सकता है।
मौसम विभाग के मुताबिक नवंबर के दूसरे सप्ताह से ठंड का असर ज्यादा महसूस हो सकता है। ग्वालियर-चंबल संभाग में उत्तरी हवाओं के प्रभाव से न्यूनतम तापमान में गिरावट की संभावना है। भोपाल, इंदौर और जबलपुर में नवंबर के दौरान बारिश की संभावना भी बनी रह सकती है। महीने के तीसरे और चौथे सप्ताह में मौसम प्रणाली सक्रिय होने पर कुछ इलाकों में फिर बारिश हो सकती है।

HighLights
5 नवंबर तक पंजाब में शुष्क मौसम रहने का अनुमान।
दिन का तापमान 32 डिग्री सेल्सियस तक पहुंचने की संभावना।
रात के तापमान में गिरावट, ठंडक बढ़ने की उम्मीद।
डिजिटल डेस्क, अमृतसर। पंजाब का मौसम आने वाले कुछ दिन शुष्क रहने का अनुमान है। इस दौरान राज्य के तापमान में अधिक बदलाव देखने को नहीं मिलगा। रातें ठंडी होंगी, लेकिन दिन का तापमान सामान्य के करीब बना रहेगा। रविवार दिन के तापमान में हल्की बढ़ौतरी देखने को मिली, जबकि ये सामान्य के करीब बना रहा।
मौसम विशेषज्ञों के अनुसार, पहाड़ों पर होने वाली बर्फबारी के कारण समतल इलाकों में चलने वाली ठंडी हवाओं से रात के तापमान में गिरावट आने का अनुमान है। मौसम विज्ञान केंद्र के अनुसार रविवार बठिंडा का तापमान सबसे अधिक रहा। वहां तापमान 32.5 डिग्री पहुंच गया। मौसम विज्ञान केंद्र के अनुसार 5 नवंबर तक बारिश की कोई खास संभावना नहीं है। पूरे सप्ताह मौसम शुष्क रहने का अनुमान है।

दिन के तापमान में रहेगी बढ़ोतरी
मौसम विभाग के अनुसार, 5 नवंबर तक पंजाब के पूर्वी और उत्तरी हिस्सों में अधिकतम तापमान 28 से 30 डिग्री सेल्सियस के बीच रहने की संभावना है। राज्य के बाकी हिस्सों में यह 30 से 32 डिग्री सेल्सियस तक रह सकता है। अधिकतम तापमान सामान्य से लेकर सामान्य से अधिक रहने का अनुमान है। इससे दिन के समय हल्की गर्माहट बनी रहेगी।
रात के तापमान में आएगी गिरावट
न्यूनतम तापमान की बात करें तो पंजाब के उत्तरी हिस्सों में यह 10 से 12 डिग्री सेल्सियस के बीच रह सकता है। पटियाला के कुछ इलाकों में न्यूनतम तापमान 14 से 16 डिग्री सेल्सियस रहने का अनुमान है। राज्य के बाकी हिस्सों में रात का तापमान 12 से 14 डिग्री सेल्सियस के बीच रह सकता है।

जानें शहरों का तापमान
पंजाब में अधिकतम तापमान की स्थिति सामान्य बनी हुई है। रविवार राज्य के औसत अधिकतम तापमान में 0.1 डिग्री सेल्सियस की हल्की बढ़त दर्ज की गई है। राज्य में सबसे अधिक तापमान बठिंडा में 32.5 डिग्री सेल्सियस दर्ज किया गया है।
इसके अलावा चंडीगढ़ में 30.1 डिग्री सेल्सियस, अमृतसर में 28.6 डिग्री सेल्सियस, लुधियाना में 30.2 डिग्री सेल्सियस और पटियाला में 30.6 डिग्री सेल्सियस रिकॉर्ड किया गया। पठानकोट और फरीदकोट जैसे क्षेत्रों में भी तापमान 28 से 30 डिग्री सेल्सियस के आसपास दर्ज किया गया है।

राजस्थान में कैसा रहेगा मौसम: दिन में बढ़ेगी गर्मी या रात में बढ़ेगी ठंड? जानें अगले सात दिन का हाल
राजस्थान में आठ नवंबर तक मौसम शुष्क रहने का अनुमान है। बारिश का अलर्ट नहीं है। दिन के तापमान में दो से तीन डिग्री तक बढ़ोतरी हो सकती है, जबकि सुबह-शाम ठंडक बनी रहेगी। बाड़मेर में अधिकतम तापमान 35.6 डिग्री और माउंट आबू में न्यूनतम 12.7 डिग्री दर्ज हुआ।
विस्तार
राजस्थान में नवंबर की शुरुआत के साथ मौसम का मिजाज बदलने लगा है। अक्टूबर के आखिरी दिनों में हुई बारिश और मेघगर्जन के बाद अब प्रदेश में आसमान साफ रहने और दिन में धूप खिलने का दौर है। रविवार को ज्यादातर शहरों में अधिकतम तापमान सामान्य से नीचे रहा, जबकि रात का तापमान सामान्य से ऊपर दर्ज किया गया। मौसम विज्ञान केंद्र जयपुर के अनुसार, अगले तीन-चार दिन ही नहीं, बल्कि आठ नवंबर तक प्रदेश के अधिकांश हिस्सों में मौसम शुष्क रहने की संभावना है। इस दौरान बारिश या आंधी को लेकर किसी जिले में विशेष अलर्ट नहीं है। साफ मौसम के बीच दिन के तापमान में मामूली बढ़ोतरी हो सकती है, जबकि सुबह और रात में ठंडक बनी रहेगी।
आठ नवंबर तक कैसा रहेगा राजस्थान का मौसम?
मौसम विभाग के पूर्वानुमान के मुताबिक, दो से आठ नवंबर तक पूर्वी और पश्चिमी राजस्थान के अधिकांश हिस्सों में बारिश की गतिविधियां थमी रहेंगी। जयपुर, अजमेर, कोटा, उदयपुर, जोधपुर और बीकानेर समेत प्रदेश के प्रमुख शहरों में मौसम साफ और शुष्क रहने के आसार हैं। इस दौरान किसी भी जिले में बारिश, आंधी या मेघगर्जन को लेकर विशेष चेतावनी जारी नहीं की गई है।
कमजोर पश्चिमी विक्षोभ के प्रभाव से कुछ इलाकों में हल्के बादल छा सकते हैं, लेकिन व्यापक बारिश के संकेत नहीं हैं। फिलहाल 15 नवंबर तक भी प्रदेश में बारिश के लिए अनुकूल परिस्थितियां बनती नहीं दिख रही हैं।

बाड़मेर में सबसे ज्यादा तापमान, माउंट आबू सबसे ठंडा
रविवार को प्रदेश में सबसे अधिक अधिकतम तापमान बाड़मेर में 35.6 डिग्री सेल्सियस दर्ज किया गया। इसे छोड़कर सभी शहरों का अधिकतम तापमान 35 डिग्री से नीचे रहा। जैसलमेर में अधिकतम तापमान 34.8 डिग्री, चित्तौड़गढ़ में 33.8 डिग्री, पिलानी में 33.1 डिग्री, फतेहपुर में 33 डिग्री और नागौर व चूरू में 32.8 डिग्री सेल्सियस दर्ज किया गया। श्रीगंगानगर में अधिकतम तापमान 32.6 डिग्री रहा।
दूसरी ओर, न्यूनतम तापमान के लिहाज से माउंट आबू सबसे ठंडा रहा, जहां पारा 12.7 डिग्री सेल्सियस दर्ज हुआ। फतेहपुर में न्यूनतम तापमान 13.9 डिग्री, सीकर में 15.5 डिग्री, अजमेर में 16 डिग्री, टोंक में 16.4 डिग्री, झुंझुनूं और चूरू में 17.5 डिग्री तथा पिलानी में 17.8 डिग्री सेल्सियस रहा।
शेखावाटी और पश्चिमी राजस्थान में रात की ठंडक कम
बारिश थमने और आसमान साफ होने के बाद प्रदेश के कई इलाकों में रात के तापमान में बढ़ोतरी हुई है। शेखावाटी के चूरू, सीकर, झुंझुनूं और फतेहपुर में न्यूनतम तापमान में इजाफा दर्ज किया गया है। वहीं, श्रीगंगानगर, बीकानेर, जैसलमेर, फलोदी और बाड़मेर सहित उत्तर-पश्चिमी राजस्थान के कई इलाकों में रात का तापमान सामान्य से दो से चार डिग्री सेल्सियस ऊपर बना हुआ है। इससे इन क्षेत्रों में रात के समय ठंड का असर अपेक्षाकृत कम महसूस हो रहा है।
जयपुर में एक सप्ताह मौसम रहेगा शुष्क
राजधानी जयपुर में रविवार को लगातार दूसरे दिन आसमान साफ रहा और धूप खिली। यहां अधिकतम तापमान 29.7 डिग्री और न्यूनतम तापमान 18.8 डिग्री सेल्सियस दर्ज किया गया। मौसम विभाग ने जयपुर में भी अगले एक सप्ताह तक मौसम शुष्क रहने का अनुमान जताया है।
भरतपुर और कोटा संभाग के कुछ इलाकों में रविवार सुबह हल्की धुंध देखने को मिली, लेकिन सूरज निकलने के साथ आसमान साफ हो गया। जयपुर, जोधपुर, अजमेर और बीकानेर संभाग में दिनभर धूप रही।
दिन में बढ़ेगा पारा, सुबह-शाम रहेगी ठंडक
मौसम साफ रहने के कारण आगामी दिनों में प्रदेश के अधिकांश हिस्सों में अधिकतम तापमान दो से तीन डिग्री सेल्सियस तक बढ़ सकता है। ऐसे में दिन के समय धूप का असर बढ़ने और गर्मी महसूस होने की संभावना है। हालांकि, सुबह और रात में अपेक्षाकृत ठंडक बनी रह सकती है।
कुल मिलाकर, राजस्थान में फिलहाल बारिश से राहत रहेगी। अगले एक सप्ताह तक मौसम शुष्क रहने और दिन के तापमान में हल्की बढ़ोतरी के आसार हैं। वहीं, रात के तापमान में उतार-चढ़ाव के बीच प्रदेश के कुछ हिस्सों में ठंडक का अहसास बना रहेगा।

यूरोप के 7 देशों के सुपरमार्केट पर साइबर अटैक:फ्रिज-फ्रीजर का तापमान 70°C तक बढ़ाया; कई देशों में हजारों किलो का खाना खराब
- कॉपी लिंक
यूरोप के 7 देशों के सुपरमार्केट के फ्रिज और फ्रीजर पर साइबर अटैक हुआ है। हैकर्स ने ऑनलाइन सिस्टम में सेंध लगाकर फ्रिज का तापमान बढ़ा दिया। इससे दुकानों में रखा दूध, मीट और दूसरी खाने-पीने की चीजें खराब हो गईं।
बेल्जियम, स्वीडन, नीदरलैंड, एस्टोनिया, लक्जमबर्ग, फिनलैंड और आयरलैंड में ऐसे मामले सामने आए हैं। बेल्जियम में कुछ स्टोर के फ्रिज का तापमान 70 डिग्री सेल्सियस तक पहुंच गया।
यूरोन्यूज के मुताबिक, ये हमले रविवार रात से सोमवार सुबह के बीच हुए। इससे पहले 12 अक्टूबर को फ्रांस के सैकड़ों सुपरमार्केट पर भी इसी तरह का हमला हुआ था।
बेल्जियम में लाखों यूरो का सामान खराब
बेल्जियम में कई सुपरमार्केट के फ्रिज का तापमान 70 डिग्री तक पहुंच गया। इससे दुकानों में रखा खाना खराब हो गया और लाखों यूरो का सामान फेंकना पड़ा।
बेल्जियम के अखबार 'ले सोइर' के मुताबिक, डेलहाइज के करीब 40, कैरेफोर के 15, इंटरमार्शे के 15 और स्पार के 5 स्टोर प्रभावित हुए। एक मीट कंपनी और मॉन्स शहर के पास मौजूद आइकिया स्टोर में भी फ्रिज सिस्टम पर असर पड़ा।
बेल्जियम के साइबर सिक्योरिटी सेंटर ने हमले की पुष्टि की है। डेलहाइज के प्रवक्ता ने बताया कि कई स्टोर के फ्रिज सिस्टम में गड़बड़ी मिली थी। कंपनी ने तुरंत जरूरी कदम उठाए, ताकि दुकानें खुली रह सकें। कैरेफोर ने भी साइबर अटैक की पुष्टि की, लेकिन कहा कि नुकसान ज्यादा नहीं हुआ।
आयरलैंड के 13 स्टोर में फ्रिज बंद पड़े
आयरलैंड की सुपरमार्केट चेन सुपरवैल्यू के 223 स्टोर में से 13 के फ्रिज सिस्टम पर हमला हुआ। कंपनी ने इन फ्रिज में रखा ठंडा और जमा हुआ खाना बिक्री से हटा दिया।
स्वीडन में आईसीए और कूप सुपरमार्केट के स्टोर भी प्रभावित हुए। वहां रात में फ्रीजर का तापमान तेजी से बढ़ गया। स्टॉकहोम के एक आईसीए स्टोर की मैनेजर ने बताया कि हमला रात करीब 2 बजे हुआ। सुबह 5:30 बजे इसका पता चला। तब तक स्टोर के सभी फ्रीजर का तापमान 50 डिग्री सेल्सियस तक पहुंच चुका था और उनमें रखा सामान खराब हो गया था।
स्वीडन के अखबार आफ्टनब्लाडेट के मुताबिक, कूप के 6 स्टोर में भी ऐसा ही हुआ। देश की साइबर सिक्योरिटी एजेंसी इन मामलों की जांच कर रही है।
नीदरलैंड में 17 कंपनियों के सिस्टम पर हमला
एस्टोनिया में सेल्वर सुपरमार्केट का एक स्टोर प्रभावित हुआ। वहां फ्रिज का तापमान 50 डिग्री सेल्सियस तक पहुंच गया।
नीदरलैंड में कम से कम 17 कंपनियों के फ्रिज और फ्रीजर को निशाना बनाया गया। हालांकि, इन कंपनियों के नाम नहीं बताए गए हैं। लक्जमबर्ग में डेलहाइज ने एहतियात के तौर पर अपना ऑर्डर सिस्टम बंद कर दिया। फिनलैंड के मीडिया के मुताबिक, वहां के कई के-ग्रुप सुपरमार्केट भी प्रभावित हुए।
फ्रिज को डीफ्रॉस्ट मोड में डालकर बढ़ाया तापमान
बेल्जियम की कंपनी सबकोबेल के CEO स्टीफन मोएलांस के मुताबिक, यह हमला फ्रांस में हुए पिछले हमले जैसा था। हैकर्स ने फ्रिज की कूलिंग यूनिट को डीफ्रॉस्ट मोड में डाल दिया। इस मोड में फ्रिज की बर्फ पिघलाने के लिए कूलिंग बंद हो जाती है। इससे तापमान बढ़ने लगा।
मोएलांस ने बताया कि इस गड़बड़ी को सिर्फ सॉफ्टवेयर अपडेट से ठीक नहीं किया जा सकता। इसके लिए फ्रिज के सिस्टम में कुछ बदलाव भी करने होंगे।
किसी हैकर ग्रुप ने जिम्मेदारी नहीं ली
आजकल सुपरमार्केट के फ्रिज और फ्रीजर को इंटरनेट के जरिए दूर बैठकर कंट्रोल किया जा सकता है। इसी वजह से इनमें खराबी आने या हैक होने पर दुकानों का पूरा सामान खराब हो सकता है।
यूरोपीय आयोग के एक प्रवक्ता ने कहा कि इन घटनाओं से पता चलता है कि साइबर अटैक का असर सिर्फ कंपनियों पर नहीं, बल्कि आम लोगों की रोजमर्रा की जिंदगी पर भी पड़ सकता है।
फिलहाल किसी हैकर ग्रुप ने इन हमलों की जिम्मेदारी नहीं ली है। फ्रांस में पिछले महीने हुए हमलों के पीछे कौन था, इसका भी पता नहीं चला है।

IMD के मुताबिक राजस्थान में नवंबर महीने के पहले दो सप्ताह मौसम शुष्क रहने और दिन का तापमान सामान्य से अधिक रहने की संभावना है. तीसरे सप्ताह पश्चिमी विक्षोभ के आंशिक असर से कुछ जिलों में हल्की बारिश हो सकती है. महीने के आखिरी सप्ताह में ठंडी हवाओं से रात के तापमान में गिरावट आएगी. हालांकि, इस बार नवंबर में कड़ाके की सर्दी पड़ने के आसार कम हैं. इधर, गुलाबी नगरी जयपुर में गुलाबी ठंड की आहट के साथ ही मोती डूंगरी गणेश मंदिर में भगवान गणेश की पूजा, भोग और शृंगार की दिनचर्या भी बदल गई है.

उत्तरी वियतनाम: उत्तरपूर्वी मानसून के और तीव्र होने की संभावना है, हनोई में तापमान 18 डिग्री सेल्सियस तक गिर सकता है।
उत्तरी वियतनाम मौसम विज्ञान एवं जल विज्ञान केंद्र के अनुसार, 3 से 5 नवंबर तक हनोई में मौसम अधिकतर शुष्क रहेगा और धूप खिली रहेगी। 5 नवंबर की रात और 6 नवंबर के दिन के दौरान एक कमजोर शीत मोर्चे के फिर से आने की संभावना है, जिससे राजधानी में छिटपुट बारिश हो सकती है।
गौरतलब है कि 8-9 नवंबर को एक अधिक शक्तिशाली शीत मोर्चा उत्तर की ओर बढ़ने की संभावना है। उत्तरपूर्वी मानसून और ऊपरी स्तर की हवाओं के अभिसरण के कारण बारिश और गरज के साथ तूफान आने की आशंका है, जिससे तापमान में काफी गिरावट आएगी।
9 नवंबर से हनोई में ठंड बढ़ने की संभावना है। बा वी और बात बात इलाकों में न्यूनतम तापमान 18 डिग्री सेल्सियस तक गिर सकता है, जबकि अन्य क्षेत्रों में आमतौर पर तापमान 19-20 डिग्री सेल्सियस रहेगा। दिन का अधिकतम तापमान लगभग 22 डिग्री सेल्सियस रहेगा।
10-11 नवंबर को हनोई में कम बारिश होने और तापमान में धीरे-धीरे वृद्धि होने का अनुमान है, लेकिन रातें और सुबहें अभी भी ठंडी रहेंगी।
उत्तरी क्षेत्र के लिए, शीत मोर्चा लगभग 6 नवंबर से प्रभावित करना शुरू कर देगा और 7-8 नवंबर को और अधिक प्रभावी होगा। तापमान में और अधिक गिरावट आने से पहले छिटपुट बारिश और गरज के साथ तूफान आ सकते हैं।
3 नवंबर को मौसम के संबंध में, राष्ट्रीय मौसम विज्ञान और जल विज्ञान पूर्वानुमान केंद्र का अनुमान है कि हनोई में न्यूनतम तापमान 24-26 डिग्री सेल्सियस और अधिकतम तापमान 30-32 डिग्री सेल्सियस रहेगा, और दिन में धूप खिली रहेगी। पूर्वोत्तर क्षेत्र में आमतौर पर रात का तापमान 23-26 डिग्री सेल्सियस रहेगा, जबकि कुछ पहाड़ी क्षेत्रों में तापमान 23 डिग्री सेल्सियस से नीचे भी जा सकता है।
वियतनाम के उत्तर-पश्चिमी क्षेत्र में न्यूनतम तापमान 21-24 डिग्री सेल्सियस रहेगा, कुछ क्षेत्रों में यह 20 डिग्री सेल्सियस से नीचे भी जा सकता है। अधिकतम तापमान आमतौर पर 28-31 डिग्री सेल्सियस के बीच रहेगा, कुछ स्थानों पर यह 31 डिग्री सेल्सियस से अधिक भी हो सकता है।
इसलिए, 3 नवंबर को उत्तर में तुरंत ठंड का प्रकोप नहीं होगा। सप्ताह के अंत से, विशेषकर 8-9 नवंबर के आसपास, तापमान में उल्लेखनीय गिरावट आने का अनुमान है।
मध्य वियतनाम: उत्तरपूर्वी हवाएं चल रही हैं, न्घे आन में बारिश हो रही है, कई क्षेत्रों को तेज आंधी-तूफान से सावधान रहना चाहिए।
मध्य वियतनाम में, 3 नवंबर को कई क्षेत्रों में बारिश और गरज के साथ तूफान जारी रहा, जबकि मध्य उच्चभूमि में 2-3 की तीव्रता वाली उत्तरपूर्वी हवाएं देखी गईं। कुछ तटीय क्षेत्र भी पूर्वी से उत्तरपूर्वी हवाओं से प्रभावित हुए।
राष्ट्रीय जल-मौसम विज्ञान पूर्वानुमान केंद्र के अनुसार, थान्ह होआ से ह्यू तक के क्षेत्र में न्यूनतम तापमान 22-25 डिग्री सेल्सियस और अधिकतम तापमान 27-30 डिग्री सेल्सियस रहेगा। दिन के दौरान छिटपुट बारिश और गरज के साथ तूफान आने की संभावना है।

न्घे आन में 3 नवंबर को बारिश बढ़ने की संभावना है। हालांकि, उत्तरी क्षेत्र की तरह सप्ताह के अंत में तापमान में अचानक गिरावट आने का अनुमान नहीं है।
क्वांग त्रि से ह्यू और दक्षिण मध्य तट तक के क्षेत्र में कुछ स्थानों पर गरज के साथ बारिश जारी है। विशेष रूप से, क्वांग न्गाई से डैक लक तक के पूर्वी हिस्से में रात के दौरान छिटपुट बारिश और गरज के साथ बारिश होने की संभावना है, और कुछ क्षेत्रों में भारी बारिश भी हो सकती है।
दक्षिण मध्य तटीय क्षेत्र में रात के समय तापमान आमतौर पर 24-27 डिग्री सेल्सियस रहता है, अधिकतम तापमान 29-32 डिग्री सेल्सियस तक पहुंचता है, और कुछ स्थानों पर 32 डिग्री सेल्सियस से भी अधिक हो जाता है।

आने वाले दिनों में, यदि ठंडी हवा का यह झोंका दक्षिण की ओर और तीव्र होता रहा, तो उत्तर मध्य क्षेत्र पर इसका अधिक प्रभाव पड़ सकता है। हालांकि, तापमान में गिरावट की सीमा और तीव्रता के बारे में अभी और जानकारी जुटानी होगी।
दक्षिणी वियतनाम: उत्तर-पूर्वी दिशा से 2-3 स्तर की हवाएं चलेंगी, हो ची मिन्ह सिटी और कई अन्य क्षेत्रों में देर दोपहर और शाम को गरज के साथ बारिश होगी।

3 नवंबर के पूर्वानुमान के अनुसार, दक्षिणी वियतनाम में न्यूनतम तापमान आमतौर पर 23-26 डिग्री सेल्सियस और अधिकतम तापमान 30-33 डिग्री सेल्सियस रहेगा, जबकि कुछ क्षेत्रों में यह 33 डिग्री सेल्सियस से अधिक भी हो सकता है।
दिन के दौरान, कई क्षेत्रों में बादल छाए रहेंगे और कुछ स्थानों पर छिटपुट बारिश और गरज के साथ तूफान आने की संभावना है। दोपहर और शाम के समय, गरज के साथ तूफान बढ़ने और पूरे क्षेत्र में रुक-रुक कर आने की संभावना है।
हो ची मिन्ह सिटी में न्यूनतम तापमान 24-26 डिग्री सेल्सियस और अधिकतम तापमान 30-32 डिग्री सेल्सियस के आसपास रहेगा। शहर के कुछ इलाकों में, विशेषकर दोपहर और शाम के समय, छिटपुट बारिश और गरज के साथ तूफान आने की संभावना है। हवाएं उत्तर-पूर्व से पूर्व दिशा की ओर चलेंगी और इनकी तीव्रता 2-3 होगी।
आंधी-तूफान के दौरान लोगों को बवंडर, बिजली गिरने और तेज हवा के झोंकों से सावधान रहने की जरूरत है।
हालांकि दक्षिण में उत्तरपूर्वी हवाएं चलने लगी हैं, लेकिन इस क्षेत्र में अभी तक उत्तर के लिए पूर्वानुमानित ठंड के कोई संकेत नहीं मिले हैं। इसके बजाय, सबसे उल्लेखनीय बदलाव दोपहर और शाम के समय गरज के साथ बारिश होना है।
आपको यह भी पसंद आ सकता है
नवंबर में 2-3 शीत मोर्चों के आने का अनुमान है, जिससे उत्तर में तापमान में उतार-चढ़ाव जारी रहेगा।
मौसम विज्ञान और जल विज्ञान विभाग द्वारा 2 नवंबर को जारी जानकारी के अनुसार, वियतनाम के उत्तरी क्षेत्र में नवंबर 2026 में 2-3 शीत मोर्चों का अनुभव होने की संभावना है।
हालांकि, उत्तरी और मध्य वियतनाम में ठंडी हवा की गतिविधि आम तौर पर कई वर्षों के औसत से कमजोर रहने का अनुमान है। देश के अधिकांश हिस्सों में औसत मासिक तापमान 1-2 डिग्री सेल्सियस अधिक रहने की संभावना है, जबकि दक्षिणी वियतनाम में यह लगभग 0.5-1 डिग्री सेल्सियस अधिक होगा।
आने वाले दिनों में सबसे महत्वपूर्ण बात यह है कि 8-9 नवंबर को उत्तर-पूर्वी मानसून के तीव्र होने की संभावना है। हनोई में 9 नवंबर से ठंड का मौसम रहने की आशंका है, और शहर के कुछ पश्चिमी इलाकों में तापमान 18 डिग्री सेल्सियस तक गिर सकता है।
ठंडी हवा के आगमन के समय, इससे प्रभावित क्षेत्र और न्यूनतम संभावित तापमान के बारे में पूर्वानुमान वास्तविक घटनाक्रम के आधार पर बदलते रह सकते हैं।

articles.full_text:
संदिग्ध हैकर्स पूरे यूरोप में सुपरमार्केट के रेफ्रिजरेटरों का तापमान बढ़ा रहे हैं।
स्वीडन और बेल्जियम से लेकर लक्ज़मबर्ग तक, कई सुपरमार्केट ने अपने कूलिंग सिस्टम के अप्रत्याशित रूप से नियंत्रण से बाहर होकर अत्यधिक गर्म होने की घटनाओं की सूचना दी है, जिसका कारण साइबर हमले होने का संदेह है।
स्वीडन में, राष्ट्रीय साइबर सुरक्षा केंद्र के निदेशक जॉन बिलो ने 2 नवंबर को पुष्टि की कि एजेंसी शीतलन प्रणाली को लक्षित करने वाली घटनाओं की एक श्रृंखला से निपटने के लिए तत्काल कार्रवाई कर रही है।
स्वीडिश रिटेल चेन आईसीए और कूप के प्रतिनिधियों ने बताया कि उनके कुछ स्टोरों में रेफ्रिजरेटर और फ्रीजर का तापमान रातोंरात अचानक बढ़ गया था। गौरतलब है कि एक स्वीडिश स्टोर ने सोशल मीडिया पर खुलासा किया कि उनके सिस्टम को फ्रांस में सैकड़ों सुपरमार्केट को प्रभावित करने वाले पिछले साइबर हमले के तापमान सेटिंग्स से मेल खाने के लिए कैलिब्रेट किया गया था।
आपको यह भी पसंद आ सकता है
इसी बीच, बेल्जियम और लक्ज़मबर्ग में अहोल्ड डेलहाइज़ के दर्जनों स्टोरों ने भी रात भर में इसी तरह की समस्याओं की सूचना दी। रेफ्रिजरेशन कंपनी सबकोबेल के सीईओ स्टीफ़न मोएलन्स ने इसका मुख्य कारण साइबर हमले को बताया।
अहोल्ड डेलहेज़ के प्रतिनिधियों ने पुष्टि की है कि वे सिस्टम के रेफ्रिजरेशन उपकरण को प्रभावित करने वाली एक "आईटी घटना" की जांच कर रहे हैं। सुपरमार्केट श्रृंखला ने पिछले महीने डच पुलिस को एक अन्य साइबर सुरक्षा घटना की भी सूचना दी थी।
स्वीडन, बेल्जियम और लक्ज़मबर्ग में हुई घटनाएं अलग-थलग मामले नहीं हैं, बल्कि फ्रांस में घटी घटना से खतरनाक समानताएं रखती हैं।
फ्रांस में सैकड़ों सुपरमार्केटों को निशाना बनाकर किए गए पिछले साइबर हमले में, हैकरों ने घुसपैठ कर स्मार्ट कूलिंग सिस्टम पर कब्ज़ा कर लिया था। डेटा चुराने या फिरौती वसूलने के बजाय, हैकरों ने कूलिंग फ़ंक्शन को निष्क्रिय करके सीधे सिस्टम को नुकसान पहुँचाया और फ्रीज़र का तापमान 50 डिग्री सेल्सियस तक बढ़ा दिया। इसके परिणामस्वरूप न केवल सभी जमे हुए खाद्य पदार्थ पूरी तरह से नष्ट हो गए, बल्कि अत्यधिक गर्मी के कारण कई प्रतिष्ठानों में आग भी लग गई।
आपको यह भी पसंद आ सकता है
विशेषज्ञों के अनुसार, यह मिलती-जुलती जानकारी बताती है कि यह कोई आकस्मिक सिस्टम त्रुटि नहीं थी, बल्कि संभवतः एक समन्वित हमला अभियान था, जिसमें एक ही प्रकार के मैलवेयर का उपयोग किया गया था या यूरोपीय खुदरा विक्रेताओं के बुनियादी ढांचा प्रबंधन प्रणालियों में एक ही सुरक्षा भेद्यता को लक्षित किया गया था।

Abstract
Heatwaves are increasingly frequent due to climate change, yet their association with respiratory sarcopenia remains underexplored. We aimed to examine the association between heatwave exposure and incident respiratory sarcopenia in a Chinese cohort, identify potentially susceptible subpopulations, and evaluate the robustness of the findings across alternative exposure definitions. In a prospective cohort study of Chinese adults from 2011 to 2015, heatwave exposure was assessed at the city level as the difference in heatwave frequency and days between 2011 and 2015 across 12 definitions (HW01-HW12). Participants free of respiratory sarcopenia at baseline were followed to identify incident cases. Logistic regression estimated odds ratios and 95% confidence intervals for the association between heatwave exposure and respiratory sarcopenia. Subgroup analyses were stratified by age, sex, BMI, geographic region, and chronic lung disease status, and sensitivity analyses evaluated the robustness of the results. Among 1984 participants, 15.7% developed respiratory sarcopenia by 2015. Greater heatwave frequency was associated with higher odds of respiratory sarcopenia in five definitions, and more heatwave days were associated with higher odds across eleven definitions. Associations appeared stronger among participants with BMI < 23 and those with chronic lung disease, while no clear effect modification was observed by age, sex, or region. Sensitivity analyses yielded broadly consistent results. Heatwave exposure was associated with higher odds of incident PEFR-based respiratory sarcopenia in Chinese adults, particularly among those with low BMI or chronic lung disease. These findings support further research on environmental heat exposure and respiratory muscle-related health, while limitations related to exposure misclassification, residual environmental confounding, and indirect outcome measurement should be considered.
Introduction
Climate change has intensified the frequency and severity of heatwaves globally, posing substantial threats to human health1,2. Epidemiological studies have linked heatwave exposure to cardiovascular and respiratory morbidity and mortality, including outpatient visits for respiratory diseases, cardiorespiratory mortality, and acute heat-related illness, particularly among older adults and people with chronic diseases3,4,5,6,7,8. Respiratory sarcopenia, characterized by reduced respiratory muscle strength with or without low muscle mass, is an emerging concern in aging populations9. It is associated with reduced lung function, frailty, and adverse clinical outcomes, yet its environmental determinants remain poorly understood10,11.
Previous research on heatwaves has mainly focused on mortality, hospitalization, respiratory symptoms, and lung function, whereas research on sarcopenia has primarily examined aging, chronic disease, nutrition, and physical function3,4,5,6,7,9,10,11,12,13. Direct studies connecting heatwave exposure with sarcopenia, especially respiratory sarcopenia, remain scarce. Heat stress may plausibly affect respiratory muscle-related health through dehydration, systemic inflammation, oxidative stress, reduced physical activity, sleep disruption, or increased ventilatory demand, but these pathways have not been well tested in population-based longitudinal cohorts3,4,5,6,8,14,15,16,17,18.
Important uncertainties therefore remain regarding whether heatwave exposure is associated with incident respiratory sarcopenia, whether any association is consistent across heatwave definitions and durations, and which groups may be more susceptible.
We aimed to investigate the association between heatwave exposure and incident respiratory sarcopenia in a prospective cohort. We also sought to identify potentially susceptible subpopulations and assess the robustness of findings through sensitivity analyses.
Methods
Population
This study utilized data from the CHARLS, a prospective, nationally representative cohort study conducted in China. A detailed description of the CHARLS project has been reported elsewhere19. In this study, the first wave of CHARLS (2011) was considered the baseline, and the third wave (2015) served as the follow-up survey. Participants younger than 45 years were excluded because CHARLS was designed to represent middle-aged and older adults in China, and respiratory sarcopenia is primarily an age-related condition. Of 25,586 initially selected CHARLS records, we excluded participants with missing sex (n = 4660), participants who could not be linked to residence or city location data (n = 4619), participants without matched city-level meteorological station information (n = 9568), participants from city_code 4100 (n = 27), participants with missing diagnostic variables for respiratory sarcopenia (n = 3628), and participants younger than 45 years (n = 111). Among the remaining 2973 participants, 989 with probable or confirmed respiratory sarcopenia at baseline were further excluded to focus on incident cases, leaving 1,984 participants in the final analytic cohort (Fig. 1). Proxy interview status was not used as an exclusion criterion in the analytic cohort. Therefore, where CHARLS permitted proxy reporting, some self-reported covariates may have been provided by proxy respondents rather than directly by participants. Due to the unavailability of participants’ exact residential addresses, environmental exposure was assessed at the city level. Table S1 illustrates the distribution of survey sites. It was assumed that participants residing in the same city shared identical exposure levels and that their residences remained relatively stable. These assumptions are partly supported by the participants’ age and China’s Hukou household registration system, although residual exposure misclassification remains possible. All participants provided informed consent, and the protocol was approved by the Ethical Review Committee of Peking University (IRB00001052-11015). The dataset used in this study is publicly available.
Covariates
The study collected baseline characteristics of participants in 2011, including age, sex, body mass index (BMI), education level, residence, geographic region (delineated by the Qinling-Huaihe line), history of alcohol consumption, smoking history, marital status, physical activity level, and presence of chronic lung disease (including asthma). Additionally, changes in BMI, alcohol consumption status, smoking status, and physical activity status were assessed over the study period to capture dynamic shifts in these key variables.
Diagnostic algorithm for respiratory sarcopenia
Respiratory sarcopenia was defined based on the current consensus that sarcopenia is a generalized muscle disorder characterized by the loss of muscle strength and mass9,12,13. Peak expiratory flow rate (PEFR) was used as a surrogate indicator of respiratory muscle strength because direct measures such as maximal inspiratory or expiratory pressure were unavailable in CHARLS. We adopted PEFR cut-off values (4.40 L/s for men and 3.21 L/s for women) proposed by a previous Asian-population study20. PEFR is clinically relevant to respiratory muscle performance but may also be influenced by airway obstruction, chronic pulmonary disease, acute respiratory status, and participant effort; therefore, the outcome in this study should be interpreted as PEFR-based respiratory sarcopenia. Appendicular skeletal muscle mass (ASM) was estimated using a validated anthropometric equation suitable for the Chinese population21,22. Multiple studies have demonstrated strong concordance between ASM equation models and dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry21,22,23. Cutoff values for low muscle mass were defined as the sex-specific values within the lowest 20% of the study population at baseline, adjusted for height (Ht) (ASM/Ht2)22,24. Probable respiratory sarcopenia was defined by the presence of a low PEFR. Confirmed respiratory sarcopenia was established in these individuals by the additional finding of low appendicular skeletal muscle mass adjusted for height (ASM/Ht2). Based on the occurrence of respiratory sarcopenia from 2011 to 2015, participants were categorized into two groups: the group with incident respiratory sarcopenia (IRS Group) and the group without incident respiratory sarcopenia (Non-IRS Group). The IRS Group included participants who developed respiratory sarcopenia during the follow-up period, progressing from no respiratory sarcopenia at baseline to either probable respiratory sarcopenia or confirmed respiratory sarcopenia. All other participants, who remained free of respiratory sarcopenia throughout the follow-up, were classified into the Non-IRS Group.
Assessment of heatwave
The meteorological data during the study period (daily average dew point temperature and daily average temperature) were sourced from the China Meteorological Administration Land Data Assimilation System (CLDAS version 2.0)25,26,27. We used the weathermetrics package in R software (version 4.4.2) to calculate the daily average heat index (HI). Since there is no standard definition for heatwaves, we defined heatwaves based on the combination of heatwave intensity and duration proposed in previous studies. Therefore, based on existing literature23, we determined the daily average HI relative thresholds (90th, 92.5th, 95th, and 97.5th percentiles) for specific cities during the study period. These thresholds were then paired with different heatwave durations: > = 2 days, > = 3 days, and > = 4 days. This combination resulted in 12 heatwave definitions (Table 1). Specifically, we calculated the change in exposure during the study period by comparing the number of heatwave days or events experienced by an individual in the 11 months prior to the interview month and the survey month in 2015 with the number experienced in the comparable period in 2011. Table 2 illustrates the changes in heatwave exposure during follow-up. Because exact residential addresses were unavailable, environmental exposure was assessed at the city level. This approach may not capture individual-level variation in indoor temperature, time-activity patterns, air conditioning use, occupational exposure, or short-term mobility. Negative values in Table 2 indicate that, for a given city-specific definition and participant interview window, the number of heatwave events or days in the 2015 exposure window was lower than that in the comparable 2011 window. These values should therefore be interpreted as within-participant changes between two survey-linked exposure windows rather than as a national monotonic trend in heatwave intensity or duration.
Statistical analysis
Baseline characteristics were summarized based on respiratory sarcopenia status (IRS Group and Non-IRS Group) and compared between participants using the chi-squared test or the Kruskal–Wallis test, as appropriate. Data are presented as means ± standard deviation (SD) or median and interquartile range (IQR) for continuous variables and percentages for categorical variables. Multiple logistic regression analyses were conducted to assess the association between heatwave exposures and binary respiratory sarcopenia status using three stepwise models. Model 1 was an unadjusted analysis evaluating the crude association. Model 2 adjusted for Covariate Set A, including age, sex, BMI, marital status, education level, residence, history of alcohol consumption, smoking history, geographic region, mean heat index, and physical activity level. Model 3 adjusted for Covariate Set B, which included all variables in Covariate Set A plus chronic lung disease, change in BMI, and changes in drinking, smoking, and physical activity status. To reduce interpretive ambiguity from multiple heatwave definitions, the main interpretation focused on the fully adjusted model and on the consistency, direction, and magnitude of associations across definitions rather than isolated significant results from individual definitions. The 95th percentile threshold lasting > = 2 consecutive days (HW07) was treated as the primary heatwave definition because it represents a commonly used high-temperature threshold while retaining sufficient exposure variability; the remaining definitions were considered robustness analyses. We performed weighted logistic regressions stratified by age, sex, BMI, geographic region, and chronic lung disease status to examine subgroup patterns. Interaction terms were tested to assess whether these associations varied across subgroups. To assess the robustness of the key findings, we conducted sensitivity analyses by excluding participants with missing baseline characteristics or standardizing age and BMI. No additional lag-period models were fitted because the exposure metric was defined over the survey month and preceding 11 months in each wave, which was intended to capture medium-term exposure before assessment. Therefore, shorter disease-latency windows or delayed effects could not be separately evaluated.
Results
Characteristics of participants
Table 3 shows the characteristics of participants by respiratory sarcopenia status. The median age of the study population was 56 years (IQR, 50–62), and 1266 (63.8%) were female. Among 1984 middle-aged to older adults, 15.7% developed respiratory sarcopenia during follow-up. Compared with participants in the Non-IRS Group, those in the IRS Group were older (median age, 58 versus 56 years), had a higher proportion of males (68.2% versus 30.2%), and were more likely to have less than lower secondary education (93.6% versus 88.0%) or chronic lung disease (15.4% versus 7.5%). Additionally, participants in the IRS Group were less likely to have a history of alcohol consumption (32.5% versus 53.0%) or smoking (30.9% versus 52.7%) than those in the Non-IRS Group.
Association between heatwave exposure and respiratory sarcopenia
Figure 2 and Figure S1 illustrate the association between heatwave exposure and respiratory sarcopenia status. In the fully adjusted model 3, greater heatwave frequency was associated with higher odds of respiratory sarcopenia across five definitions [odds ratio (OR) 1.120, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.033–1.214 for HW07; OR 1.127, 95% CI 1.026–1.238 for HW08; OR 1.128, 95% CI 1.012–1.258 for HW09; OR 1.136, 95% CI 1.031–1.253 for HW10; OR 1.199, 95% CI 1.049–1.369 for HW11] (Fig. 2A). Similarly, an increase in heatwave days was associated with higher odds of incident respiratory sarcopenia across eleven definitions (OR 1.017, 95% CI 1.004–1.030 for HW01; OR 1.017, 95% CI 1.003–1.032 for HW02; OR 1.014, 95% CI 1.001–1.027 for HW03; OR 1.026, 95% CI 1.011–1.042 for HW04; OR 1.025, 95% CI 1.009–1.041 for HW05; OR 1.025, 95% CI 1.010–1.041 for HW06; OR 1.021, 95% CI 1.007–1.036 for HW07; OR 1.019, 95% CI 1.005–1.034 for HW08; OR 1.018, 95% CI 1.004–1.033 for HW09; OR 1.019, 95% CI: 1.004–1.034 for HW10; OR 1.020, 95% CI: 1.004–1.037 for HW11) (Fig. 2B). Given the use of multiple heatwave definitions, these results should be interpreted primarily as evidence of a consistent exposure–response pattern rather than as independent findings for each definition. The associations were generally more consistent for heatwave days than for heatwave events, suggesting that the duration or cumulative burden of heat exposure may be more informative than event counts alone. However, because definitions combined both percentile thresholds and minimum duration criteria, the results should be interpreted as patterns across related exposure metrics rather than as evidence that a single duration threshold is uniquely causal.
Impact of heatwave exposure on respiratory function and muscle mass
Figure 2C and D illustrate the association between heatwave exposure and change in PEFR. In the fully adjusted model 3, greater heatwave frequency was associated with lower PEFR under several definitions (estimate = 0.959, 95% CI 0.924–0.996 for HW02; estimate = 0.912, 95% CI 0.861–0.966 for HW10; estimate = 0.899, 95% CI 0.831–0.973 for HW11; estimate = 0.885, 95% CI 0.801–0.979 for HW12) (Fig. 2C). Similarly, an increase in heatwave days was associated with lower PEFR under several definitions (estimate = 0.991, 95% CI 0.983–0.999 for HW02; estimate = 0.988, 95% CI 0.979–0.997 for HW04; estimate = 0.986, 95% CI: 0.977–0.995 for HW05; estimate = 0.989, 95% CI 0.980–0.998 for HW06; estimate = 0.991, 95% CI 0.982–0.999 for HW07; estimate = 0.990, 95% CI 0.981–0.999 for HW09; estimate = 0.989, 95% CI 0.979–0.998 for HW10; estimate = 0.989, 95% CI 0.979–0.999 for HW11) (Fig. 2D). However, the impact of heatwaves on muscle mass appeared less pronounced (Figure S2). In the fully adjusted model 3, greater heatwave frequency was associated with lower muscle mass under only two definitions (estimate = 0.912, 95% CI 0.847–0.982 for HW01; estimate = 0.887, 95% CI 0.797–0.987 for HW02) (Figure S2A), while its impact appeared less evident across the remaining definitions. These analyses support a possible role of lung-function-related pathways, but they do not establish mediation or causality.
Subgroup analysis and sensitivity analysis
To identify subpopulations potentially susceptible to heatwave exposure, we performed subgroup analysis of the associations between heatwave exposure and the odds of respiratory sarcopenia, stratified by age, sex, BMI, geographic region, and chronic lung disease status (Table S2–11). Compared with participants with a BMI of 23 or higher, those with a BMI below 23 showed stronger positive associations between increased heatwave exposure and respiratory sarcopenia risk [estimate = 0.311, 95% CI 0.078–0.545 versus estimate = − 0.112, 95% CI − 0.359–0.135 for HW12 (events)] (Table S6). Participants with chronic lung disease also appeared more susceptible to heatwave exposure [estimate = 0.147, 95% CI 0.025–0.270 versus estimate = 0.007, 95% CI − 0.040–0.053 for HW01 (events); estimate = 0.180, 95% CI 0.000–0.361 versus estimate = − 0.005, 95% CI –0.074–0.064 for HW02 (events); estimate = 0.186, 95% CI − 0.016–0.387 versus estimate = − 0.026, 95% CI − 0.123–0.071 for HW05 (events)] (Table S10). No clear effect modification by age, sex, or geographic region was observed. Sensitivity analyses showed that the association between heatwave exposure and respiratory sarcopenia remained broadly consistent after excluding participants with missing baseline characteristics (Fig. 3A and B) or standardizing age and BMI (Fig. 3C and D).
Conclusion
This prospective cohort study found that increased heatwave exposure, assessed as the difference between 2011 and 2015, was associated with higher odds of incident PEFR-based respiratory sarcopenia. Subgroup analyses suggested that individuals with BMI < 23 and chronic lung disease may be more susceptible. Additional analyses showed that heatwave exposure was more consistently associated with PEFR than with estimated muscle mass, which is compatible with, but does not prove, a lung-function-related pathway.
These results add to environmental epidemiology evidence that extreme heat is associated with adverse respiratory outcomes. Prior studies have reported associations between heatwaves and respiratory outpatient visits, respiratory mortality, and declines in lung function, often attributing these patterns to heat-related airway inflammation, oxidative stress, dehydration, and increased ventilatory workload3,4,5,6,7,8. In contrast, the sarcopenia literature has focused mainly on aging, chronic disease, nutrition, and physical function rather than climate-related exposures9,10,11,12,13. Our study connects these two areas by examining PEFR-based respiratory sarcopenia as an outcome potentially sensitive to environmental heat exposure, while recognizing that the observational design precludes causal inference.
A potential biological explanation is that heat stress may impair respiratory function through dehydration, systemic inflammation, oxidative stress, or increased ventilatory demand, thereby reducing respiratory reserve without necessarily causing measurable loss of appendicular muscle mass (Fig. 4)16,17,18. Participants with BMI < 23 may have lower physiologic reserve, while those with chronic lung disease may experience greater airway resistance, hypoxemia, or respiratory workload during heat events. However, because inflammatory biomarkers and direct measures of respiratory muscle strength were unavailable, this pathway should be interpreted as a hypothesis rather than a demonstrated mechanism.
From a public health perspective, the findings suggest that heatwave adaptation strategies may need to consider respiratory muscle-related vulnerability in addition to conventional cardiorespiratory outcomes. Cooling interventions, air quality protection, and clinical monitoring during extreme heat may be especially relevant for individuals with low BMI or chronic lung disease. These implications should be interpreted cautiously given the observational design and the possibility of residual confounding.
Key strengths of this study include its prospective design, the focus on incident respiratory sarcopenia over four years, and the evaluation of multiple heatwave definitions. The inclusion of PEFR and estimated muscle mass analyses provided additional context for interpreting whether the observed associations were more closely linked to respiratory function or muscle mass. Subgroup and sensitivity analyses also helped assess whether findings were consistent across participant characteristics and analytic assumptions.
Several limitations should be noted. First, PEFR was used as a surrogate indicator of respiratory muscle strength because direct measures such as maximal inspiratory pressure, maximal expiratory pressure, or respiratory muscle endurance were unavailable. PEFR can be influenced by chronic lung disease, airway obstruction, acute respiratory conditions, and participant effort, which may have introduced outcome misclassification. Second, heatwave exposure was assessed at the city level rather than the individual level, which may have introduced exposure misclassification because indoor temperature, cooling access, occupational exposure, time-activity patterns, and short-term mobility were not captured. Third, the study period overlapped with a period of severe haze pollution in China. Air pollutants such as PM2.5, ozone, and nitrogen dioxide may co-vary with heat and independently affect lung function; insufficient control for these environmental confounders may have biased the observed associations. Fourth, proxy interview status was not an exclusion criterion. Although objective measurements such as PEFR were obtained through standardized assessment procedures, some self-reported covariates may have been proxy-reported, which could introduce reporting bias or nondifferential misclassification of health status, behaviors, and socioeconomic characteristics. Fifth, the observed effect sizes were relatively small; consequently, the associations may be sensitive to residual confounding, exposure or outcome misclassification, and other unmeasured sources of bias. Sixth, although participants with respiratory sarcopenia at baseline were excluded, reverse causality cannot be fully ruled out because individuals with poorer baseline lung function, greater frailty, or chronic disease may have been more vulnerable to heatwave exposure and more likely to develop respiratory sarcopenia. Seventh, the use of multiple heatwave definitions increases the possibility of chance findings; therefore, the results should be interpreted according to the consistency of patterns across definitions and the prespecified primary definition rather than isolated statistical significance. Eighth, inflammatory biomarkers were unavailable, limiting mechanistic interpretation. Ninth, we did not explicitly model lag times between heatwave exposure and respiratory sarcopenia onset; the exposure window reflected the survey month and preceding 11 months, and shorter latency periods could not be distinguished. Finally, large-scale climate variability, including El Nino/La Nina events, may have influenced year-to-year heatwave patterns but was not explicitly modeled.
Future research should incorporate direct measurements of respiratory muscle strength, inflammatory biomarkers, individual-level and time-varying residential heat exposure, air pollution data, explicit lag structures, large-scale climate variability indicators such as El Niño-Southern Oscillation, and repeated annual exposure measures to clarify temporal and biological pathways. Studies in diverse populations are also needed to assess generalizability and to determine whether lung function decline mediates the association between heatwave exposure and respiratory sarcopenia.

‘Climate change led to over 10,000 additional preterm births in India, Bangladesh and the Philippines during the April 2024 heatwave’: ZCA
Human-driven climate change is causing an increase in preterm births across South and Southeast Asia, putting newborns at risk of mortality and lifelong health impacts, according to a new analysis by Zero Carbon Analytics (ZCA)—an international research group providing insights and analysis about climate change and the energy transition.
This is the first analysis to estimate preterm births linked to the April 2024 heatwave in these countries, including their distribution within each nation, assessing how continued global warming could affect the burden in India and Bangladesh by mid-century, says the ZCA statement
Advertisement
The analysis estimates that climate change caused 10,600 additional preterm births across India, Bangladesh and the Philippines during the extreme heatwave in April 2024—an event made at least 45 times more likely by human-caused global warming.
Advertisement
In India, Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, West Bengal and Jharkhand accounted for around two-thirds of this excess burden, the analysis said, projecting that the country could experience more than 15,000 additional preterm births during a typical April by mid-century.
Uttar Pradesh is expected to have the largest absolute burden, followed by Bihar and Rajasthan, researchers say.
The 10,600 preterm births—8,830 in India, 1,479 in Bangladesh and 263 in the Philippines—would not have occurred in a world without human-caused warming, they add
The April 2024 heatwave was associated with approximately 16,150 additional preterm births compared with a typical April—an increase of 3.6% in India, 11.9% in Bangladesh and 10% in the Philippines—as per the researchers.
The findings also highlight the disproportionate impact on countries that have contributed little to historical greenhouse gas emissions but face greater climate risks and have fewer resources to adapt.
Preterm birth is the leading cause of neonatal mortality globally and is associated with long-term physical, neuro-developmental and socioeconomic consequences. As it is, the three countries have high preterm birth rates and are now disproportionately exposed to climate-driven extreme heat.
Ahead of COP31, with health among its priorities, this comes as another grim reminder
The UN Climate Chief has called for action on climate-driven heat affecting pregnancy and childbirth, describing it as a potentially fatal new faultline in the climate crisis.
Dr Joanne Bentley-McKune, lead author and senior research analyst at ZCA, said extreme heat was increasing the risk of preterm births and associated lifelong health impacts. The study estimated that more than 16,000 additional births occurred during April 2024 compared with a typical April, over 10,000 of which were attributable to human-caused warming.
Professor Rashmi Agarwalla, Nodal Officer, Climate Change, Department of Community and Family Medicine, AIIMS Guwahati, said maternal heat protection must become integral to health-system preparedness, antenatal care and community-based maternal services. Anaemia, poor nutrition and prolonged outdoor work compound heat-related risks for pregnant women and newborns, particularly in vulnerable communities, she added.
Despite these risks, heat remains an overlooked threat to maternal and neonatal health as per Prof Agarwalla.

As extreme heat intensifies around the world, the World Health Organization (WHO), the World Meteorological Organization (WMO), Unicef and the United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA) have launched the first-ever set of priority indicators to help countries track the health impacts of heat on pregnant women, newborns and children.
The new framework is designed to strengthen preparedness, improve monitoring, and accelerate response, the WHO said, adding that these actions help protect populations most vulnerable to climate-related health risks.
Studies show that exposure to extreme heat can harm health from pregnancy to childhood, leading to a 26 per cent increase in the odds of preterm birth. Newborns are increasingly exposed, with babies under one year experiencing 389 per cent more heatwave days in 2024 compared with the 1986-2005 baseline period. Globally, an estimated 1.5 billion children are exposed to heatwaves, which are becoming more frequent, longer or more severe.
The new report recommends that countries monitor preterm births, stillbirths, low birthweight, pregnancy hypertension, child deaths and health facility visits during extreme heat. Monitoring school attendance can also help reveal how heat is disrupting children’s lives.
As extreme heat is fast becoming a common feature of a warming world, the WHO is calling on countries to strengthen their ability to monitor and respond to its health impacts. By using the new priority indicators, governments can better identify risks, target interventions and protect pregnant women, newborns and children from preventable harm, it said.

Researchers tracked more than 285,000 adults across Finland and the UK to investigate how chronic disease and socioeconomic disadvantage influence the health risks of extreme temperatures, with implications for protecting vulnerable populations as the climate warms.
Study: Health risks of hot and cold temperatures in people with pre-existing conditions and social disadvantage. Image Credit: Quality Stock Arts / Shutterstock
People with both clinical and socioeconomic vulnerabilities experienced more than tenfold higher excess mortality associated with extreme heat or cold than those with neither or only one vulnerability, according to a new study published in the journal Nature Communications.
Background
Global warming has increased extreme heat events worldwide, while extreme cold events have generally become less frequent, raising concerns about their public health effects. During heat and cold exposures, the human body maintains core temperature through sweating and vasodilation (widening of blood vessels) and through vasoconstriction (narrowing of blood vessels) and thermogenesis, respectively.
These regulatory processes can be impaired by preexisting health conditions, further increasing the risk of temperature exposure-related morbidity and mortality in affected people. Similar to preexisting health conditions, socioeconomic vulnerabilities, such as living in households with poor insulation or ventilation, are known to influence the health impact of temperature exposure. However, direct individual-level evidence on how clinical and socioeconomic vulnerabilities affect temperature exposure-related morbidity and mortality remains limited in the literature.
The current study aimed to assess health risks during extreme heat and cold exposures among people with clinical and socioeconomic vulnerabilities.
Key findings
The researchers analyzed individual-level data from 275,763 Finnish adults and 9,681 UK adults. They compared mortality rates in both cohorts and emergency hospital visit rates in Finland during extreme heat, cold, and moderate-temperature periods. Clinical vulnerability was defined using 17 chronic diseases or disease groups, including diabetes, cancer, and cardiovascular and kidney conditions. Social vulnerability was determined from neighborhood-level deprivation scores rather than individuals' incomes or housing conditions.
Extreme temperatures were defined as the hottest and coldest 2.5% of seven-day periods in each cohort. Finnish data showed that seven-day average ambient temperatures above 20.4 °C or below –11.4 °C were associated with 1.4-fold and 1.1-fold higher mortality rates, respectively, than moderate temperature exposure (–11.4 to 20.4 °C). The estimated increase in cold-related mortality in Finland was not statistically significant in the main analysis. The UK cohort showed similar patterns.
In both Finnish and UK datasets, excess mortality associated with hot and cold periods combined was more than tenfold higher among individuals with both clinical and social vulnerability than among those with neither or only one vulnerability. This subgroup included 15,326 Finnish and 354 UK participants, leaving some subgroup estimates imprecise.
Excess temperature-associated mortality differed little between individuals with neither vulnerability and those with only one vulnerability.
Climate modeling of the potential effects of future global warming suggested that an increase from approximately 1°C to 4°C could raise the proportion of deaths attributable to extreme temperatures from about 1% to more than 5%, roughly a fivefold increase in both Finland and the UK.
In the Finnish cohort, data on non-fatal outcomes showed that compared to moderate temperature exposure, cold periods were associated with a 9% lower rate of emergency hospital visits, whereas hot periods were associated with a 5% higher rate of such visits. The observed associations were stronger among individuals with both clinical and social vulnerability than those with neither vulnerability or only one vulnerability. Cold weather may also restrict access to emergency care, potentially contributing to fewer recorded visits.
Bars show the proportions of primary causes of death among participants who died during cold, moderate, and hot periods in FPS and the Whitehall study. Differences in these proportions between periods were tested using two-sided chi-squared tests. No differences in cause-specific mortality were observed across temperature periods in either study. Supplementary Table 2 presents data for all underlying and contributing causes of death and largely replicates these findings, with one exception: respiratory and genitourinary deaths were more common during cold periods in FPS but not Whitehall.
Study significance
The study reveals that people with both clinical and socioeconomic vulnerabilities experienced substantially greater excess mortality associated with extreme temperatures. Climate projections suggest that as warming progresses, increases in heat-related mortality could outweigh reductions in cold-related mortality.
Overall, the findings suggest that exposure to extreme temperatures may accelerate deaths among highly vulnerable individuals who already have a high short-term mortality risk. Heat and cold may act as acute stressors that worsen pre-existing or subclinical illnesses in vulnerable populations. The researchers also acknowledged that temperature extremes may cause premature deaths among people without either identified vulnerability.
The observed association between social vulnerability and extreme temperature-related mortality may reflect differences in the ability to avoid temperature-related physiological stress. Socioeconomically deprived people may be more likely to live in households with poor insulation and ventilation and have limited access to heating, cooling, and safer environments. These housing-related explanations were proposed by the researchers, but individual household conditions were not directly measured.
The study associated higher temperatures with increased rates of emergency hospital visits for infectious and digestive diseases. Warmer conditions may promote pathogen survival and replication, but the researchers did not directly test this mechanism.
Emergency hospital visits for skin, neurological, and mental disorders, and for external causes, also increased with higher temperatures, while respiratory-related visits were less frequent. These findings are biologically plausible. Extreme hot and humid conditions increase sweating and dehydration and promote bacterial and fungal skin infections. The researchers suggested that heat-related aggression, impulsivity, and frustration may contribute to self-harm, violence, and accidents, without establishing the mechanisms behind psychiatric visits.
These findings highlight the need for developing public health strategies to protect vulnerable people from adverse health outcomes during extreme weather conditions.
The results reflect climatic and socioeconomic conditions in Finland and the UK. Further research is needed to validate these findings in populations living in markedly different climatic, geographic, or socioeconomic conditions.
The analyzed datasets include occupational cohorts and are not fully representative of the general populations of the UK and Finland. Because unemployed people and those with work disabilities were excluded at baseline, the participants are generally healthier than the overall population. These factors may have led to an underestimation of the adverse health effects of extreme temperatures. The climate modeling also did not account for future demographic changes, shifts in environmental conditions, or protective adaptations that might alter temperature-related health risks. As the study was observational, the reported associations cannot establish that temperature exposure directly caused the estimated excess deaths.

Thunderstorms are forecast to return to south-east Queensland on Tuesday.
The storms could be severe, with large hail and heavy rain possible.
A severe heatwave is forecast for the Gulf country, with temperatures reaching 40 degrees.
More thunderstorms are looming for south-east Queensland this week, as the state's north sweats through severe heatwave conditions.
After a mostly fine day on Monday, the Bureau of Meteorology warns of possible severe storms for the Sunshine Coast, Brisbane and the Gold Coast on Tuesday.
Senior meteorologist Steve Hadley said November was "peak storm season".
"Over the next few days, thunderstorm risk continues over many parts of Queensland," he said.
"In fact, it ramps up over south-eastern parts of the state on Tuesday.
"We're looking at more widespread thunderstorms and some more possibly severe storms."
The afternoon storms could bring large hail, damaging winds and heavy rain which may lead to flash flooding, particularly after the deluge some areas received in the past two weeks.
The regions predicted to be hit include the Darling Downs, the Gold Coast, Brisbane and the Sunshine Coast.

Some years bring severe droughts while other years bring heavy rainfall. One contributing natural climate phenomenon that influence these patterns is El Niño weather conditions.
According to Disaster and Emergency Management Services (DEMS) in the City of Ekurhuleni, this weather pattern inculcates extreme heatwave, negatively affecting existing open water stream sources to dryness, intense moisture evaporation, and when it rains, excessive thunderstorms accompanied by strong winds and hail, with possibilities of damage to structures and vegetation.
In instances of dryness, the temperature quantifies extreme high levels of heat above average, measured either in degrees Celsius ( C), Fahrenheit ( F) or Kelvin systems.
Elevated temperatures soar well above normal, raising the threat of severe heatwave, heat-related illnesses and increased water evaporation from dams, rivers streams, and soil subjecting vegetation to dryness. Possibilities of veld fires are high in the middle of the summer season.
These elevated temperatures affect winds and atmospheric circulation, with possibilities of drastic change in rainfall patterns and reduced summer season rains.
El Niño distorts weather patterns into extremes of severe droughts or violent floods. DEMS stated it fundamentally alters human lives, health and societal stability. It triggers a domino effect directly affecting human survival.
Due to El Niño 2026/2027 summer season, DEMS shared the following safety information:
Health emergencies and heat illnesses:
Severe heatwaves exceeding 35 C to 40 C and above directly trigger heat exhaustion, heat stroke and cardiovascular stress.
Such temperatures aggravate chronic medical conditions which might result in loss of lives.
Outdoor workers, children, athletes and the elderly face life threatening medical conditions.
Dehydration:
It is a physical condition that occurs when the body loses more fluids and water than it takes in. The imbalance disrupts the delicate balance of essential electrolytes. Body cells, tissues and organs cannot carry their normal metabolic processes.
Sign and symptoms:
Thirst
Sticky or dry mouth
Polyuria (frequent urination)
Dark yellow concentrated urine
Dizziness
Confusion
Rapid heart rate
Fainting.
Heat exhaustion:
Clinical syndrome by body overheating, typically due to prolonged exposure to high temperatures accompanied by severe dehydration from heavy sweating.
The body loses excessive water and essential salts known as electrolytes straining the cardiovascular system.
Heavy, profuse sweating
Rapid weak pulse
Dizziness, light-headedness
Nausea, vomiting, or loss of appetite
Muscle cramps or weakness
Cool, pale and clammy skin
Headache and intense thirst.
Heat stroke:
It is the shutting down of the body’s internal cooling system whereby the body core temperature rises to 40 C or above. This severe overheating can rapidly damage life sustaining organs such as the brain, heart and kidneys.
Signs and symptoms:
Hot and dry skin
Fast and strong pulse rate
Nausea
Rapid shallow breathing
Vomiting
General treatment:
Drink water to rehydrate
Drink sports drinks to replace electrolytes
Do not wait until you feel thirsty to consume fluids
Outdoor personnel should drink one cup of cool water every 15 to 20 minutes
Outside workers in hot weather conditions must balance heat dissipation with essential safety and sun protection
Eye protection requires balancing light radiation filters, fog resistance and heat ventilation
In case of emergency, move the person to a cooler area, loosen clothing and have them sip cool water or an electrolyte drink if conscious
Apply cold, wet towels to the neck
Avoid carbonated or fizzy drinks.
Avoid drinking alcohol or caffeine drinks
Prevent children from playing in a hot environment
Refrain from strenuous activities
Affected patients require hospitalisation for further medical treatment.
For life-threatening emergencies, call 011 458 0911 (charged at normal call rates), 10177 (toll free from a land line) or dial 112 (free from any cellphone).

The Lagos State Government has warned residents to prepare for possible extreme heat, dehydration, and heatstroke, pointing to an emerging El Niño climate pattern and the transition into the dry season.
The government said Lagos could be particularly exposed because of its dense population, rapid urbanisation and concentration of buildings and roads that absorb and retain heat.
It consequently urged residents, employers and schools to take precautionary measures before conditions worsen.
The Commissioner for the Environment and Water Resources, Tokunbo Wahab, issued the warning on Friday, saying changing climate patterns and seasonal conditions could bring unusual temperatures, dry spells, dust, and increased discomfort across the state.
In a statement obtained from the Lagos State Government’s information channels by The PUNCH, Wahab said that although the severity and local impact of the conditions would depend on prevailing weather patterns, residents should not wait for extreme conditions to emerge before preparing.
He said, “The strengthening El Niño climate pattern, alongside the seasonal transition into the dry season, could contribute to unusual temperature conditions, increased heat discomfort, dry spells, dust and deteriorating air quality.
“Although the intensity and local impact of these conditions would depend on prevailing weather patterns, residents must take the emerging climate risks seriously and prepare adequately.”
Wahab said Lagos’s urban landscape could intensify the effects of rising temperatures, particularly in densely populated neighbourhoods and informal settlements where buildings, roads and other infrastructure absorb heat, while limited green spaces and poor ventilation offer little relief.
“The concentration of buildings, roads and other heat-absorbing infrastructure, coupled with limited green spaces and inadequate ventilation in some neighbourhoods, could intensify temperatures in built-up areas,” he said.
The commissioner warned that prolonged exposure to excessive heat could cause dehydration, heat exhaustion and heatstroke, with potentially serious consequences if not treated promptly.
He identified children, older persons, pregnant women, outdoor workers, street traders, construction workers, waste handlers and people with underlying health conditions as particularly vulnerable.
He urged families, employers, schools and community leaders to pay special attention to these groups and ensure that protective measures were available to reduce their exposure.
The government also warned that rising temperatures could compound Lagos’s existing air-quality problems, particularly during the dry season when dust and haze may worsen respiratory irritation.
Wahab said people living with respiratory conditions could experience aggravated symptoms, while increased dependence on petrol- and diesel-powered generators during power interruptions could further deteriorate air quality in some communities.
He urged residents to avoid open burning of refuse and adopt measures to reduce exposure to heat and polluted air.
“Residents are advised to drink sufficient water regularly, wear lightweight and breathable clothing, seek shade and well-ventilated spaces, and reduce strenuous outdoor activities during the hottest periods of the day,” he said.
He also called on schools, markets, workplaces and other public facilities to provide adequate ventilation, drinking water and shaded areas where people could take breaks.
Wahab urged residents to recognise the symptoms of heat-related illnesses, including excessive sweating, dizziness, headache, weakness, nausea and muscle cramps, and to move anyone experiencing them to a cooler environment for immediate cooling assistance and medical attention where necessary.
He warned that sudden collapse or loss of consciousness should be treated as a medical emergency requiring immediate attention.
“Residents with respiratory conditions are also advised to limit exposure to dusty environments and follow relevant health and air-quality advisories,” he added.
Beyond individual precautions, the commissioner called for coordinated action by government agencies, health institutions, businesses, environmental experts and community stakeholders to strengthen preparedness.
He urged residents and businesses to protect existing trees, plant more trees, preserve green spaces, dispose of waste properly and discourage activities that contribute to environmental degradation.
Wahab said the state government, through the Ministry of the Environment and Water Resources and its agencies, would continue public awareness efforts and work with the Nigerian Meteorological Agency, the Lagos State Ministry of Health and the Lagos State Emergency Management Agency to strengthen preparedness and response to emerging environmental risks.

Pune rain brought relief from several days of intense October heat on Monday, while heavy showers affected the city, suburbs and parts of Pune district and the India Meteorological Department issued a yellow alert for Maharashtra. The alert covers parts of Konkan and central Maharashtra, where thunderstorms and heavy rain are expected over the next 24 to 48 hours.
Rain began late on Sunday night and continued into Monday morning, with intermittent showers reported across Pune. The downpour affected central peth areas as well as Shivajinagar, Hadapsar, Kothrud, Aundh, Baner, Balewadi, Warje, Sinhagad Road, Katraj and Kondhwa.
Water accumulated at several locations after the sudden spell of heavy rain, according to the report. The showers also brought cooler conditions after days of oppressive heat, providing relief to residents across the city and its surrounding areas.
The weather system was not limited to Pune city. Heavy rain was also reported in parts of the district, including Baramati, Indapur, Ambegaon, Junnar and Jejuri, along with other talukas. The rain comes as parts of the state face concerns over dry conditions and water availability.

It did not specify the individual reservoirs, the volume of additional storage or the current live storage position.
For residents, the immediate impact is likely to be on road conditions, local travel and visibility during intense spells. Water accumulation was reported at several points, but the report did not mention major traffic disruptions, injuries, structural damage or official emergency measures by civic authorities.

Pune is expected to remain cloudy, with light to moderate showers possible over the following hours. Residents have been advised to remain alert as the yellow alert remains in effect.

The National Institute of Meteorology and Hydrology (NIMH) has issued a red alert for heavy rainfall in five Bulgarian districts on Tuesday, November 3, with precipitation potentially exceeding 65 liters per square meter, while a second Mediterranean cyclone is expected to bring more than 100 liters per square meter in some locations, according to Meteo Balkans.
The red warning covers Dobrich, Varna, Smolyan, Kardzhali, and Haskovo. An orange alert for significant rainfall is in force across almost all other districts, where totals could range from 35 to more than 55 liters per square meter. A yellow rainfall warning applies to Sofia-City, Sofia Province, Vidin, Pernik, and Kyustendil.
The NIMH forecast calls for cloudy skies across the country over the next 24 hours, with occasional rain in some areas overnight. Winds will be light to moderate from the east-northeast, turning northerly in Eastern Bulgaria. Minimum temperatures will be between 5°C and 10°C, reaching 13°C-15°C along the Black Sea coast and standing at around 6°C in Sofia.
Rain is expected across nearly the entire country on Tuesday, with snowfall in the mountains. Precipitation will intensify and become significant in volume. The wind will remain moderate from the east-northeast, strengthening in Eastern Bulgaria during the second half of the day. Maximum temperatures will range from 6°C to 11°C in most areas, reaching 14°C-16°C in the southeast and along the coast, while Sofia will see around 8°C.
Meteo Balkans said the second Mediterranean cyclone would maintain rainy conditions, with the heaviest precipitation expected in Southern and Central Bulgaria and parts of the east. Cloud cover will remain extensive overnight, bringing mostly light to moderate intermittent rain to many areas, while heavier downpours are forecast in the far northeastern districts.
After midnight, a new precipitation zone linked to the approaching cyclone will begin strengthening over Southwestern and Southern Bulgaria. Winds will reach moderate speeds, coming from the east-northeast, while northerly winds will prevail in Eastern Bulgaria.
Rainfall totals could exceed 70-80 liters per square meter in some locations, with local amounts potentially surpassing 100 liters. The precise distribution will depend on the cyclone's movement and how long precipitation zones remain over individual areas.
Earlier rainfall has already raised soil moisture levels in affected regions, reducing the ground's capacity to absorb further precipitation. This could cause water to run off more quickly toward low-lying areas, rivers, and ravines.

The combination of precipitation, wind, and poor visibility will make hiking conditions unfavorable.
Rain will continue across other mountain ranges, falling at lower elevations and turning to snow above approximately 1,600 meters. Fresh snow will accumulate at higher altitudes. Extra caution is advised in the Rila and Rhodope mountains, where heavy rainfall could quickly raise water levels in mountain rivers and ravines, particularly where the ground is already saturated.

Alejandro Balde ready to quit Barcelona in January as stinging Hansi Flick criticism puts Man Utd on red alert
Barcelona left-back Alejandro Balde is increasingly open to leaving Camp Nou during the upcoming winter transfer window after falling down the pecking order under head coach Hansi Flick. The 23-year-old's mounting frustration has placed several Premier League suitors including Manchester United on alert ahead of a potential January move to England.
Spanish defender considers winter exit
Balde has accepted that he must depart his boyhood club to secure regular starting minutes and rebuild his confidence, according to Mundo Deportivo. Despite defensive injuries handing him substitute outings against Paris Saint-Germain, Real Madrid and Alaves, he is yet to start this term behind Joao Cancelo and Xavi Espart. Coaching staff believe the defender suffers from concentration lapses and misjudges when to press.
Blunt public assessment hurts academy graduate
Ahead of Saturday's meeting with Alaves, Flick delivered a harsh assessment of the defender: "Balde currently lacks the confidence he needs in his game, as well as the conviction. And defenders are crucial."
Those comments contrasted sharply with the German's earlier supportive tone on September 15, when he stated: "I am happy with him and everyone. We have three players in every position. Managing all of that is the most difficult part."
One month later on October 16, the boss had similarly remarked: "It's not an easy situation for him, but he is training very well, which is the first thing he needs to do. In that position, we have Espart and Cancelo. Surely it is not ideal for Balde, but he works professionally, which is what I want. In that situation, you have to prove you are ready, and he is doing that."
Respected team-mates challenge tactical decisions
Balde feels particularly aggrieved after learning of his peripheral status through media briefings, unlike Marc Casado and Hector Fort, who received direct calls from Flick. Having spent 16 years at the club, the defender's frustration grew when senior team-mates questioned tactical drills that displaced him from his natural position. While positional rival Cancelo has surprisingly emerged as a vocal dressing-room ally, Balde remains determined to avoid the career stagnation experienced by close friend Ansu Fati, welcoming a departure structure similar to Ronald Araujo's.
Permanent deal demanded by Blaugrana
Both Manchester clubs enquired about Balde last summer alongside Bayern Munich, and the defender remains keen to test himself in England as United monitor his situation. Unless his minutes improve dramatically before the new year, the 23-year-old will actively listen to mid-season proposals. However, because Barcelona require funds to reinvest defensively rather than sanctioning a loan, Premier League suitors must finance a permanent transfer.
